As the  five family members of the Respondent-husband/(
 Respondent No.1) named above are arraigned as  accused persons / respondents / opposite  parties in various pending legal proceedings  and are not physically present in-person at the  time of signing of this Settlement Agreement  due to their age, distance and /or ailments,
 the Respondent-husband/( Respondent No.1) has  signed this Settlement agreement on behalf of  4 all five accused persons/ respondents /
opposite parties, i.e. Mr. Krishan Jivan Rastogi (Respondent No.2), Mrs. Laj Rastogi (Respondent No.3), Mrs. Shobha Rastogi (Respondent No.4), Mr. Krishan Murari Rastogi &
Mr. Sumit Rastogi.

The Petitioner-wife understands the same and agrees that the terms and conditions in this settlement agreement are qua all the five family members of the Respondent-husband/( Respondent No.1) who were earlier arraigned as accused persons /
respondents / opposite parties in the currently pending litigations.
17. The said parties hereby have agreed that the terms of this Settlement agreement are irrevocable and unquestionable.

The said parties undertake that this Settlement agreement would inter alia be legal, valid,
binding, enforceable and executable in all manners and none of the parties shall be at liberty to take the advantage of any technical language or lacuna, if any.

18. Default clause: The said parties mutually agree that in case, one party fails to adhere to the terms and conditions of this Settlement agreement at any point of time, then in that eventuality, the other party shall be at liberty to exercise appropriate legal remedies against the defaulting party and/or their family members for breach of such terms/
stipulations/ undertaking given in this Settlement agreement.

The appropriate legal remedies that can be taken recourse to by the Anshika Rastogi vs Atin Rastogi on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21142024/

said parties and/or their family members, would not be limited to contempt of court proceedings under The Contempt of Courts Act, 1971.

19. The said parties declare that they have agreed on each and every term recorded in this settlement agreement, after carefully reading over and fully understanding and appreciating the contents, scope and effect thereof, as also the consequences of the breach thereof.

5 20. The said parties hereby unequivocally agree,
accept and confirm that the present Settlement Agreement has been read and understood by them and further that they have put their signatures hereunder voluntarily out of their own free will and consent, without any force, fraud,
pressure, fear, compulsion, undue influence or coercion, without misrepresentation or mistake from either side knowing fully their legal rights.

21. The said parties agree, accept and confirm that they are fully aware of the present terms in this Settlement Agreement, and that they have been made aware of the same in English as well as their vernacular language i.e. Hindi,
by their respective legal advisors / counsels/
advocates, of the full consequences and effects thereof.

22. Further to jointly signing this Settlement Agreement, the said parties agree and undertake to move a Joint Interlocutory Application titled Seeking Dissolution of Marriage by mutual consent Under Article 142(1) Of The Constitution to request the Honble Apex Court to quash / dispose all the pending cases mentioned in para 3 of this Settlement Agreement and to dissolve their marriage by mutual consent, as provided under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
The said parties agree to move this Joint Interlocutory Application supported by their respective affidavits, within 10 working days of signing of this Settlement Agreement.

23. All the documents related to this settlement - Settlement Agreement, Joint Interlocutory Application under Article 142 of the Anshika Rastogi vs Atin Rastogi on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21142024/
5 Constitution of India and supporting affidavits of the said parties, etc. will be signed by the said parties on the date of signing of this Settlement Agreement.

Further, the said parties will co-operate, and when absolutely required make themselves available before the Honble Apex Court, on the hearing date of the Joint Application u/s Article 142.

 6  24.

The said parties agree and undertake that,
 they will not misuse anywhere and for any  purpose - the electronic evidence such as audio  and video recordings, WhatsApp chats, Photos  and E-mail conversations, Marriage and identity  related documents such as Passport, Pancard,
 Driving License, Marriage Registration  Certificate, Photographs (passport size and  marriage photos), Educational Certificates, any  other documents and signature samples, after  signing this Settlement Agreement and after  obtaining the Decree of Divorce.

25 . While the proceedings of quashing / disposal  of all pending litigations and the dissolution  of marriage are pending in the Honble Apex  Court, the said parties agree and undertake not  to take any precipitative steps against the  other party and/or their family members in any  of the pending legal proceedings..
6.
We have taken the Joint Application and Settlement Agreement dated 28.01.2025 on record.

Having considered the matter in detail and having perused the Settlement Agreement & Joint Application, we are of the view that this is a fit case for this Court to exercise its power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India to dissolve the marriage between the parties.
Consequently, the marriage between the parties which was solemnized on 07.10.2014 at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh stand dissolved by a decree of divorce by mutual consent.
